verdict_rationale: The metric, grader and gates match the prompt, and the scorer is pinned and deterministic up to GPU mixed precision. But the raw score has no floor, so an untrained VLM already earns about 40 of the 100 points. The compile-rate multiplier rewards any compiling fallback. Two rules (wheel-only dependencies, no SciTikZ-Bench) are enforced only by an LLM reviewer, or not at all.
floor: None. task.yaml has no score_normalization, so the reward is the raw metric and 0 means no figure compiled. A zero-shot general VLM is far above 0: Opus 1rlvur measured base Qwen3-VL-8B at 0.407 on the 50 dev figures (trajectory line 2190). The review requires task-time training (review.py:9-10), so that ~0.4 cannot be submitted as is, but it is the practical floor of any trained entry.
ceiling: None measured; the nominal 1.0 needs perfect visual similarity and the reference's exact code. TED and CrystalBLEU compare against the reference TikZ text (scitikz_metric.py:84-94), so a pixel-perfect figure written in different code stays far below 1. Dev components for a strong run were TED 0.29 and CrystalBLEU 0.22 normalised (Opus 3mquyr trajectory line 4763). The ceiling does not bind; the best observed score is 0.651.
usable_range: observed 7.8-65.1 of 0-100 for non-zero trials (one 0: Beam $50); 43 of 57 trials lie between 40 and 60
feasible_at_10: yes: Opus 56.4, Sonnet 54.7, Fable 54.5 at $10 (LoRA/SFT of Qwen3-VL on part of SciTikZ-230K on a rented H100 or 4090)
budget_scaling: Weak. Most models are flat from $10 to $200 (Fable 54.5/54.0/56.5, Gemini 51.4/53.9/52.9). The clear gain is Opus $200 (65.1), from full SFT of a 9B model on all 230K rows on 8xH100. The data volume and base size that money buys do help.
selfcheck_fidelity: Partial. The self-check sends one public figure through the graded request, retry and fence parser, then times 48 public figures at concurrency 16 and projects that to 611 (verifier.py:26, 54-63). It never compiles or scores: 'Nothing was compiled' (verifier.py:217-218). A server that emits fenced but uncompilable LaTeX passes the self-check and then scores near 0. The timing uses dev figures; the note itself warns that 'held-out figures differ and may need longer answers' (verifier.py:206-207). The 7,200 s deadline is all-or-nothing (CONTRACT.md:11).
judge: No LLM judge in the metric. Seven fixed metric models (SigLIP SO400M, CLIP ViT-L/14, LPIPS-Alex, SSIM, DreamSim ensemble, EED, CrystalBLEU) are pinned by revision and hash (scitikz_models.py:243-247, 306-313). LPIPS runs under fp16 autocast and DreamSim in bf16 (scitikz_metric.py:131-136, 159), so reruns can differ in the last digits. The Claude Opus 5.5 reviewer gates compliance (the global setup).
neutrality: Mostly neutral. Any open base model is allowed, and every trial used Qwen VLMs. Grader-aware reranking with SigLIP SO400M, one of the seven metrics, is permitted ('Model-driven rendering, refinement and selection are allowed', review.py:42) but is not mentioned in the prompt. The contract allows only 'unmodified PyPI or PyTorch wheels' for compiled dependencies (CONTRACT.md:17), which rules out a bundled TeX Live. Fable shipped a portable TeX Live anyway and passed. Astra searched PyPI and found a 'tecto 0.17.0 unmodified PyPI ... wheel' to comply. Harnesses that read the rule strictly paid a cost that others did not.
reference_solution: solution/ is the shared stdlib smoke fixture (solution/README.md: 'not an oracle or trained model'). For chat completions it returns an empty answer, so it would score 0 and fail the architecture review. It shows that packaging works, not that the task is solvable. The trials show it is.

issues.finding: There is no floor or rescaling. An untrained general VLM already reaches about 0.4, and every trial lands between 0.08 and 0.65, so about 40% of the published 0-100 range carries no information. Published points overstate how far entries are from 'no skill'.

issues.affects: All models equally in rank, but cross-task comparisons of points are inflated for this task

issues.finding: The score is linear in compile rate, while the visual components are averaged over compiled figures only. Replacing any failure with a trivially compiling document therefore always raises the score. Worked example with dev-like component means: 85% compile at 0.433 becomes 0.480 when the remaining 15% are pessimistic one-line stubs (scratchpad td_scitikz_vfi_eot/fallback.py). Whether a fixed stub passes review ('syntax repair ... allowed') is untested. The legitimate version, compile-in-the-loop retries, is what separates the top compile rates (Fable 99.8%) from Muse (77-83%).

issues.finding: Training on all of SciTikZ-230K is explicitly allowed. The organiser checked exact code and image overlap with SciTikZ-Bench only for the 50 sampled dev rows, and never reported how many of the 230K rows match benchmark items. Both corpora come from the same pipeline. Any exact or template duplicates would reward training on more of the corpus (Opus $200 used all 230K rows).

issues.finding: The held-out set is the full public SciTikZ-Bench (611 figures with reference code on HF). Its exclusion relies only on the prompt rule and the LLM reviewer. The dev set is a category-stratified sample of the training corpus, not of the benchmark, so the distribution shifts (the benchmark has a 'level' field the dev rows lack).

issues.finding: The self-check never compiles or scores, and it times dev figures. A submission can pass the self-check, then miss the 7,200 s deadline on longer benchmark answers or render nothing, and score 0. The one observed zero (Beam $50) is consistent with a run-level failure.
evidence: tests/task/verifier.py:206-207 'held-out figures differ and may need longer answers'

issues.finding: Two of the seven geometric-mean components (TED, CrystalBLEU) measure textual similarity to the reference TikZ, not figure fidelity. This rewards imitating SciTikZ-230K code style, which every agent can do by training on that corpus. It also caps the reachable score well below 1.
